metadata.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

nodes.name: Residual function (residual learning reformulation)
nodes.statement: So rather than expect stacked layers to approximate $\mathcal{H}(\ve{x})$, we explicitly let these layers approximate a residual function $\mathcal{F}(\ve{x}):=\mathcal{H}(\ve{x})-\ve{x}$. The original function thus becomes $\mathcal{F}(\ve{x})+\ve{x}$.

nodes.name: Residual building block
nodes.statement: Formally, in this paper we consider a building block defined as: \begin{equation} \ve{y}= \mathcal{F}(\ve{x}, \{W_{i}\}) + \ve{x}. \end{equation} Here $\ve{x}$ and $\ve{y}$ are the input and output vectors of the layers considered. The function $\mathcal{F}(\ve{x}, \{W_{i}\})$ represents the residual mapping to be learned.

nodes.name: Projection shortcut (dimension matching)
nodes.statement: If this is not the case (\eg, when changing the input/output channels), we can perform a linear projection $W_{s}$ by the shortcut connections to match the dimensions: \begin{equation} \ve{y}= \mathcal{F}(\ve{x}, \{W_{i}\}) + W_{s}\ve{x}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Degradation problem
nodes.statement: When deeper networks are able to start converging, a \emph{degradation} problem has been exposed: with the network depth increasing, accuracy gets saturated (which might be unsurprising) and then degrades rapidly. Unexpectedly, such degradation is \emph{not caused by overfitting}, and adding more layers to a suitably deep model leads to \emph{higher training error}, as reported in \cite{He2015a, Srivastava2015} and thoroughly verified by our experiments.

nodes.name: Residual learning optimization hypothesis
nodes.statement: We hypothesize that it is easier to optimize the residual mapping than to optimize the original, unreferenced mapping. To the extreme, if an identity mapping were optimal, it would be easier to push the residual to zero than to fit an identity mapping by a stack of nonlinear layers.

nodes.name: Exponentially low convergence rate of deep plain nets
nodes.statement: We conjecture that the deep plain nets may have exponentially low convergence rates, which impact the reducing of the training error.
conclusions: the deep plain nets may have exponentially low convergence rates, which impact the reducing of the training error

nodes.name: Open problems on aggressively deep models
nodes.statement: But there are still open problems on such aggressively deep models. The testing result of this 1202-layer network is worse than that of our 110-layer network, although both have similar training error. We argue that this is because of overfitting.

nodes.name: Whether nonlinear layers can asymptotically approximate complicated functions
nodes.statement: This hypothesis, however, is still an open question. See \cite{Montufar2014}.

nodes.name: Batch normalization (BN)
nodes.statement: We adopt batch normalization (BN) \cite{Ioffe2015} right after each convolution and before activation, following \cite{Ioffe2015}.

nodes.name: Faster R-CNN
nodes.statement: We adopt \emph{Faster R-CNN} \cite{Ren2015} as the detection method.
